title: Keyspace resilience: cache lifespan sculpting and staged rollback checklist
creator: Asha R. Patel
description:
Goal: Produce an actionable, low-risk runbook and automation for recommending cache key design and cache-lifespan (time-to-live) profiles that reduce token spend while preserving output quality and latency SLOs. This ticket covers: hit-rate modeling methodology (sample-based and production-shadow experiments), automated candidate generation for key transformations (affixing, namespace bucketing, suffix stripping), adaptive lifespan annealing schedules, cost/latency trade-off heuristics, and a staged apply/rollback checklist with observable triggers.

Scope and deliverables:
- Hit-rate modeling doc: sampling strategy, feature set (prefix length, user cohort, sequence-length bucket, request age), and target metrics (net hit lift, false-positive churn, tail latency).
- Key transformation engine prototype: ruleset that suggests conservative key rewrites plus confidence scores and expected unit-cost delta.
- Lifespan annealing scheduler: automated policy that gradually increases cache lifespan for candidate keys with pass/fail thresholds based on budget and quality gates.
- Safe apply and rollback checklist & automation: shadow-canary stages, traffic split recipes, revert hooks (automated and manual), and alert thresholds tied to real-time SLOs and cost burn.
- Observability artifacts: saved queries and dashboards for hit-rate, per-key miss amplification, token cost delta, per-route latency p95/p99, and regression alerts.

Success criteria:
- Recommend changes that achieve >= 12% median per-token cost reduction on targeted workloads without increasing 99th-percentile latency by > 5% or increasing error rate.
- Automated staged apply path that can fully revert within 15 minutes if a quality or latency regression is detected.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the existing KV runtime or eviction policy. This is recommendations + safe orchestration only.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Over-aggressive key coarsening can cause miss amplification and higher upstream compute cost; mitigate via conservative confidence thresholds and cost-sanity checks.
- Longer lifespans bias toward stale KV entries for dynamic content; mitigate via cohort-aware lifespans and expiry variance.

Open questions:
1) Should we prefer namespace bucketing (per-customer) or request-affixing (per-session) as the default for multi-tenant routes? Proposal: default to namespace bucketing for authenticated, high-value tenants and affixing for low-identifying endpoints.
2) What is the minimum sample size for reliable hit-rate uplift predictions? Initial experiment uses 1M requests or 48 hours of traffic, whichever comes first.

Next steps:
- Spike: run sample-based hit forecast on 3 routes (chat-streaming-high, embeddings-bulk, rerank-low) and produce candidate key transforms. (Owner: Liam, 2w)
- Implement annealing scheduler prototype and connect to safety hooks in Console (Owner: Asha, 3w)
- Draft runbook and alert thresholds; review with SRE and PM. (Owner: Liam, 1w)
